inputs.original_text: Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan has firmly rejected those allegations of Rs 700 crore corruption tied to the Cooperative Department’s proposed common software project, insisting the claims are politically driven. This is just another calculated smear from forces invested in preserving economic inequality, aimed at derailing any institutional reforms that might empower cooperatives to better support workers, small producers, and marginalized communities against exploitation. These attacks distract from the real need to strengthen public systems that challenge entrenched power rather than letting the privileged sabotage progress for the vulnerable.
inputs.modified_text: Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan is rejecting those allegations of Rs 700 crore corruption tied to the Cooperative Department’s proposed common software project and insists the claims are politically driven. This is the standard leftist dodge we see whenever these politicians get caught pushing big-government schemes that expand state control and drain public resources. Rather than defend traditional family businesses and personal responsibility, they hide behind talk of challenging "entrenched power" while building up collectivist institutions that undermine cultural continuity and national values. We should focus on holding leaders accountable for waste and graft instead of letting them smear critics to protect their ideological experiments that weaken social order.
